messages:
Erin: follow-up on the packaging/upgrade RFC. we ran a small on-prem soak and observed a new failure pattern during rolling upgrades: partial image writes + operator fast-fail cause repeated rollbacks on nodes behind intermittent network links. proposing a lightweight transactional staging layer to reduce flip-flop.

Joel: can you describe the failure sequence you saw?

Erin: brief flow: 1) operator requests bundle, 2) proxy begins streaming into temp area, 3) operator validates manifest but activation starts before all shards are pinned, 4) node fails health-check (IO spike), operator marks activation failed and triggers immediate cleanup, 5) proxy GC reclaims some temp shards before retry, next attempt sees missing shards and repeats. a small timing window causes churn.

Sana: sounds similar to classic TOCTOU. what are you thinking for staging?

Erin: idea: introduce a three-state activation: STAGE -> VERIFY -> CUTOVER. STAGE streams and pins to a namespaced staging store (not yet visible to runtime). VERIFY runs streaming crypto checks and checksum proofs (Merkle or chunk-hash) and resolves inter-bundle dedupe. only when VERIFY succeeds do we move to CUTOVER by atomically switching a symlink or pointer.

Marcus: that would prevent runtime from seeing half-applied bundles. good. downside is disk pressure during STAGE. for air-gapped clusters with limited scratch space this could be an issue.

Joel: can we make STAGE incremental and bounded? meaning allow staging to pin up to X% of available scratch and fail early with clear metrics so operator can evict lower-priority staging jobs.

Erin: yes. operator would expose staging_quota_per_node and a staging_eviction_policy (LRU/priority). also a prepare_priority hint in the activation request. that lets critical services jump the queue.

Sana: what about GC interactions? proxy should honor a staging-lease header so GC doesn't evict shards that are in STAGE. two approaches: signed short-lived lease embedded in activation request, or a lightweight per-node lease table in the proxy.

Marcus: signed-lease has advantage of avoiding central state but means the proxy must validate signatures. in air-gapped installs verifying using a static admin key is OK. per-node lease table is simpler if your deployment already has a central ops-plane.

Erin: hybrid option: signed-lease by default, plus an optional poll endpoint for long-running preps where operator can re-advertise leases if it survives a restart. leases include prepare-id, node-id, expiry, and chunk-list fingerprint.

Joel: we should also address partial rollback semantics. if an activation fails and we cleanup staging data, the operator should delay marking the node as needing rollback for a small backoff window to allow transient IO issues to clear. propose soft-fail state 'quarantine' where operator retries N times with exponential backoff before full rollback.

Sana: add metric quarantine_count and quarantine_retry_successes. ops will want alerting when quarantines spike.

Marcus: compatibility: older proxies/operators expect single-phase activation. plan: feature-flagged STAGE flow with clear opt-out. API extension is minimal: add POST /v1/activation with mode=stage|direct and optional prepare_priority, staging_quota_hint, lease_signature.

Erin: security note: staging exposes more surface area (signed manifests, chunk lists). we must ensure verification is strict and provide an allowlist option for customers who cannot distribute signer keys. include a doc for offline key provisioning.

Joel: another performance note: do streaming verify while writing to staging to fail fast. crypto CPU will spike; we should make verify pluggable (SHA256, blake2). also expose a config to limit concurrent verify threads per node.

Sana: opsbot: schedule a small staging canary?

ops-bot: canary-schedule: staging clusters A/B tomorrow 04:30 UTC. feature-flag=staging-activation. monitor: prepare_latency, quarantine_count, staging_disk_pressure.

Erin: action items I will take: 1) sketch RFC addendum with sequence diagrams and API drafts; 2) prototype signed-lease prototype and a minimal proxy skip on lease; 3) add metrics and an operator soft-fail/quarantine state; 4) run 48h staging canary and collect resource/IO profiles.

Marcus: add a migration note for private customers: provide a '--staging-temp-dir' option and an explicit disk quota check at startup. also an admin tool to inspect pending staging namespaces and force-clean them if needed.

Joel: and include a rollback mitigations section: how to detect stuck prepares and safe manual recovery steps. customers hate opaque 'failed' state with no guidance.

Sana: +1. if RFC lands, let's also prepare a short KB for solutions engineers and customers explaining tradeoffs.

build-bot: ci: created branch rfc/staging-activation-addendum-621111.

Erin: thanks everyone. I'll open PR and ping for review. :sparkles:
